# New Telemetry traits and the young-player weight rule

Date: 2026-10-17. Status: **decisions recorded; build in 020.** Nothing in
019 changed.

## What Telemetry added

Read from the live leaderboard Columns panel (2026, all 11 groups, both tabs)
on 2026-10-17. Advanced Stats: no change. Player Traits: 7 new columns.

| Group | New Player Traits columns |
|---|---|
| OT, IOL | Pull Agility, Perimeter Speed |
| OB-LB | Closing, Reaction Time |
| CB, SAF | Targeted Coverage, Closing, Reaction Time |

Telemetry's own definitions (player-page tooltips):

| Trait | Definition |
|---|---|
| Pull Agility | Measures a lineman's ability to change direction and cut upfield as a puller. |
| Perimeter Speed | Measures a lineman's straight line speed. |
| Targeted Coverage | Measures the primary coverage defender's ability to stay in phase when targeted. |
| Closing | Measures a defender's ability to close on the ball when it's in the air, both as the primary and secondary defender. |
| Reaction Time | Measures how fast a secondary defender commits to the ball once it's thrown. |

LB tooltips were not read separately; assumed the same text.

**Sample size:** these traits are blank for many players. On the OT board,
4 of the top 15 have no Pull Agility / Perimeter Speed. One 2026 CB ranked
"14th of 36 in FBS" on Reaction Time, so very few players are scored.

## Effect on the pipeline today

- `check_exports.py` flags only missing columns, so the new columns pass.
- `scripts/powerquery/Stage.m` keeps only its known column list, so the new
  columns are dropped silently. Nothing breaks; nothing is used.

## Crosswalk (proposed; add as secondaries, not counted traits)

Counted traits drive elite share (same open question as Elusiveness), so
these go in as secondaries until that is decided.

| Group | Trait | Baylor factor (000 GRD SCALE) | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| OT | Pull Agility | Athletic Ability | Factor had no Telemetry feed (no CoD/Decel for OL). |
| OT | Perimeter Speed | Speed (Play-speed) | Colleague proposed Foot speed / Redirect. The definition is straight-line speed, so Speed. Speed had no OL feed. |
| OG/C | Pull Agility | Pulling / 2nd level blocking | Direct match. |
| OG/C | Perimeter Speed | Speed (Play-speed) | As OT. |
| CB, STAR | Targeted Coverage | Man-to-Man Coverage | Direct match. |
| CB, STAR | Closing | Ball Skills | "Disruptive at rec. point." |
| CB, STAR | Reaction Time | Ball Skills (secondary) | No read/react factor on CB. |
| SAF | Reaction Time | Key & Diagnose | "Reads and reacts quickly." |
| SAF | Closing | Range | Plays to the sideline. |
| SAF | Targeted Coverage | none clean | Info only until staff decide. |
| LB | Closing | Lateral quickness / Range | Weak fit. |
| LB | Reaction Time | none | LB scale has no read/react factor. Info only. |

Defensive rows are proposed by Claude, not yet confirmed by Eric or staff.

## Weight rule for young players (Eric chose option 1, 2026-10-17)

Height stays the hard line. A player whose only size miss is weight below the
SETTINGS floor, with Elig. 3 or more, is flagged **PROJECT** instead of
scoring Size 1 (critical deficiency). Older players keep the current rule:
a light senior is not a project.

Before building: read the SIZE (data) formula in 019 to confirm how a
below-floor weight scores today (1 or 3). The 000 matrix weight columns were
unclear in the text export. `check_workbook.py` does not recompute SIZE, so
spot-check SIZE and the PROJECT flag on a few players per position.

## Build list for 020

1. Stage.m and POSITION MAP: add the 7 columns (OT, IOL, OB-LB, CB, SAF).
2. CROSSWALK / glossary: add the rows above, with the definitions.
3. SIZE: weight-only miss + Elig. >= 3 -> PROJECT, not 1.
4. `check_exports.py`: add the new columns to EXPECTED only after a full
   2023-2026 pull shows whether older seasons carry them.

# AGENTS.md

Project: PP_Recruiting (Baylor Football Player Personnel)

## What this is

A unified grading system for Baylor Football player personnel that couples
Telemetry (Teamworks) trait percentiles with the internal S.T.A.Q.S. grading
scale, so transfer-portal data gets filtered down to the players who deserve a
scout's time. The STAQS grade stays the grade of record. Telemetry data only
decides who gets reviewed. It never produces a competing grade.

## Two locations, know which is which

Workbooks, Word deliverables and the `Send/` folder live on Google Drive:

`G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\02_SPORTS\Football\PP_Recruiting`

That folder holds the full project handoff in its own `AGENTS.md` and the
development history in `LOG.md`. Read both before doing work on the system
itself. They are the substantive spec. This repo is the version-controlled half:
documentation, decisions, and scripts.

An older copy of the project under `OneDrive - Baylor University` no longer
exists. Session logs and Codex rollouts that name that path are stale.

## Session routine

- Start: run `git pull`, then read `docs/STATUS.md` before doing anything else.
  Then read the Drive folder's `AGENTS.md` and `LOG.md`.
- End: update `docs/STATUS.md` (done, next, open questions), commit, and
  `git push`.
- Never leave uncommitted work at the end of a session.

## Conventions

- Durable notes and decisions go in `docs/`, committed. Not in chat.
- Workbooks, documents and data exports stay on Google Drive, not in this repo.
  Files over 95 MB never go in git.
- Telemetry and Teamworks are read-only. Navigate and read, never edit there.
- Writing: plain, direct, no em dashes. Documents use the Baylor design system.
- Deliverables on Drive are numbered in sequence. 013 is the latest, so the next
  one is 014. `docs/STATUS.md` holds the current number.
- The proposed Jev recruiting pilot is captured in
  `docs/2026-09-22-jev-recruiting-pilot.md`. It is a shadow-mode plan, not an
  approved workbook rule or a replacement for the weekly refresh.

## Standing rules carried over from the Drive handoff

- Threshold flags, never a weighted composite.
- Elite share, not raw elite count, because positions carry different trait
  counts (OL has 2, LB has 8).
- The data grades 4 of 5 critical factors, proxies Toughness, and never touches
  FBI, wiring, keep-ability, character, or medical.
- Do not retry reading Telemetry's auth token or importing its internal service
  classes. Both are blocked. Scrape the rendered table instead.

## Telemetry's definitions

I read these from the pop-ups on the player pages.

- **Pull Agility:** a lineman's ability to change direction and cut upfield as a puller.
- **Perimeter Speed:** a lineman's straight-line speed.
- **Targeted Coverage:** how well the main coverage defender stays with his man when the ball comes his way.
- **Closing:** how well a defender closes on the ball while it is in the air.
- **Reaction Time:** how fast a defender in the secondary (CB or safety) commits to the ball after the throw.

## Where they go

- **O-line:** Pull Agility goes where your colleague said: Athletic Ability for OT, and Pulling / 2nd level for OG.
- **Perimeter Speed should change.** It measures straight-line speed. So it goes in **Speed (Play-speed)**, not Foot speed. Foot speed in our scale means mirroring a rusher. The O-line Speed factor also has no Telemetry data today, so this fills an empty factor.
- **CB:**
  - Targeted Coverage goes to Man-to-Man Coverage.
  - Closing and Reaction Time go to Ball Skills.
- **SAF:**
  - Reaction Time goes to Key & Diagnose.
  - Closing goes to Range.
  - Targeted Coverage has no clean factor.
- **LB:**
  - Closing is a weak fit for Lateral quickness / Range.
  - Reaction Time has no factor. Our LB scale has no "read and react" factor.
